title: No Blue without Red: Evolutionary Properties of Super-Early Galaxies
comment: 17 pages, 6 Figures. Submitted to the Open Journal of Astrophysics. Comments welcome
summary: The discovery of numerous luminous, super-early galaxies at $z>10$ by JWST has revealed a striking diversity in their ultraviolet (UV) properties, ranging from extremely blue, dust-poor systems to a smaller population of significantly reddened sources. We investigate the physical origin of this diversity within the framework of the Attenuation-Free Model (AFM), in which radiation-driven outflows redistribute dust to large galactic radii, reducing the effective attenuation. Applying the model to a sample of 32 spectroscopically confirmed super-early galaxies, we derive their key physical properties, including halo mass, star formation efficiency, metallicity, and outflow extent. We find that these systems reside in massive halos ($\log M/M_\odot \sim 10.7$) and exhibit moderate ($0.01 \lesssim ε_* \lesssim 0.05$) star formation efficiencies, while frequently reaching super-Eddington conditions that trigger powerful outflows. Within this framework, we propose an evolutionary sequence in which galaxies transition from a dust-obscured ``Red Monster'' phase to a UV-bright ``Blue Monster'' phase as outflows clear their central regions. The recently confirmed red galaxy EGS-z11-R0 at $z=11.45$ is naturally interpreted as a system observed during this obscured phase. Compact ($r_e \lesssim 150$ pc) sources are instead difficult to reconcile within AFM; we speculate that their emission is dominated by an AGN. Our results provide a unified interpretation of super-early galaxy properties and highlight the key role of radiation-driven outflows in shaping galaxy evolution at cosmic dawn. Future observations with JWST and ALMA will be essential to test these predictions and further constrain the nature of the earliest galaxies.

AI.tldr: JWST's discovery of diverse UV properties in super-early galaxies ($z>10$) is explained by the Attenuation-Free Model (AFM), where radiation-driven outflows redistribute dust, causing galaxies to transition from red, obscured ("Red Monster") to blue, UV-bright ("Blue Monster") phases. The red galaxy EGS-z11-R0 at $z=11.45$ is a key example of the obscured phase, while compact sources ($r_e \lesssim 150$ pc) may be AGN-dominated.
AI.motivation: To understand the physical origin of the striking diversity in UV properties (extremely blue vs. significantly reddened) observed in luminous super-early galaxies at $z>10$ by JWST.
AI.method: Applied the Attenuation-Free Model (AFM) — where radiation-driven outflows remove dust from central regions — to 32 spectroscopically confirmed super-early galaxies, deriving halo mass, star formation efficiency, metallicity, and outflow extent.
AI.result: Galaxies reside in massive halos ($\log M/M_\odot \sim 10.7$) with moderate star formation efficiencies ($0.01 \lesssim ε_* \lesssim 0.05$) and frequently reach super-Eddington conditions. An evolutionary sequence from "Red Monster" (dust-obscured) to "Blue Monster" (UV-bright) phases is proposed. Compact sources ($r_e \lesssim 150$ pc) are difficult to explain with AFM and may be AGN-dominated.
AI.conclusion: Radiation-driven outflows play a key role in shaping galaxy evolution at cosmic dawn, providing a unified interpretation of super-early galaxy properties. Future JWST and ALMA observations are needed to test these predictions.

title: Evidence of radial-migration driven Galactic disc expansion with the U-shape stellar age profile
comment: submitted to Nature Astronomy, comments are warmly welcome
summary: Canonical theory predicts galaxies grow "inside-out", producing their observed negative radial age gradient. This picture is challenged by galaxies' `U-shaped' colour profiles -- indicating reversed age gradient -- explained by either outside-in formation or radial migration. Extragalactic observations cannot disentangle these two possibilities, but temporally and spatially resolved observations in the Milky Way offer a solution. Here we report a more complex U-shaped age profile of the Milky Way extending to 20 kpc, featuring an outer positive gradient followed by an age plateau of $\sim$5 billion year beyond 12 kpc. Age and chemical abundance distributions of outer disk stars rule out outside-in formation and confirm radial migration as the primary driver of the outer positive age gradient and plateau. Our results suggest local star formation in the Galaxy truncates around 12 kpc and radial migration has expanded the Milky Way far beyond its native star formation regime out to 20 kpc -- a growth mode likely common to disk galaxies. The Milky Way thus provides a critical template to understand disk assembly in external galaxies, improving our understanding of galaxy growth.

AI.tldr: The Milky Way's disk exhibits a U-shaped age profile extending to 20 kpc, with an outer positive age gradient and a ~5 Gyr age plateau beyond 12 kpc. Chemical abundances rule out outside-in formation and confirm radial migration as the main driver, indicating star formation truncates around 12 kpc while migration extends the disk to 20 kpc — a growth mode likely common to disk galaxies.
AI.motivation: To resolve whether the U-shaped colour profiles (indicating reversed age gradients) observed in external galaxies arise from outside-in formation or radial migration, using temporally and spatially resolved Milky Way data.
AI.method: Analysis of the Milky Way's radial age profile and chemical abundance distributions of outer disk stars out to 20 kpc, comparing predictions of outside-in formation versus radial migration scenarios.
AI.result: The Milky Way shows a complex U-shaped age profile: outer positive gradient and a ~5 Gyr age plateau beyond 12 kpc; chemical abundances rule out outside-in formation and support radial migration as the cause.
AI.conclusion: Radial migration, not outside-in formation, drives the outer age gradient and plateau. Star formation truncates around 12 kpc, and migration expands the Milky Way beyond its native star-forming zone to 20 kpc — a mode likely common to disk galaxies, providing a template for understanding external disk assembly.

title: Suppression of star formation at the centre of barred AGN galaxies
comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 2 tables
summary: We measured the Concentration (C) index of Hαand CO (J = 2-1) in 17 nearby star-forming galaxies from the PHANGS survey. We have found four barred spiral galaxies with a C(Hα)/C(CO) ratio of ~ 0.3-0.4, while the other 13 galaxies exhibit ratios of ~ 1 (range from 0.7 to 1.3). All four barred galaxies with low ratios host active galactic nuclei (AGNs), consistent with a scenario in which star formation is suppressed by mechanical and radiative feedback from the AGN. Therefore, negative feedback is effective in these four barred galaxies with a low molecular gas mass fraction (< 0.1), even when AGN activity is relatively weak. The formation of bar structures causes molecular gas to collect in the central region, leading to starburst activity. However, after the starburst, the remaining gas becomes inefficient for star formation rapidly due to AGN feedback. It can mean the quenching process occurs more rapidly in AGN-barred galaxies. Furthermore, since gas remains in the central region, AGN activity is likely to continue. These quenching processes are a unique mechanism found in barred spiral galaxies and are essential to understanding galaxy evolution.

AI.tldr: This paper measures the concentration indices of Hα and CO in 17 nearby star-forming galaxies, finding that four barred spiral galaxies with AGNs show suppressed star formation (C(Hα)/C(CO) ~ 0.3-0.4) compared to typical galaxies (~1). Negative AGN feedback rapidly quenches star formation in these barred galaxies with low molecular gas fractions, suggesting a unique quenching mechanism in barred spirals that is important for galaxy evolution.
AI.motivation: To investigate the role of AGN feedback in suppressing star formation in barred spiral galaxies, and to understand how bar structures and AGN activity together influence the quenching process in galaxy evolution.
AI.method: Measured the Concentration (C) index of Hα and CO (J = 2-1) emission in 17 nearby star-forming galaxies from the PHANGS survey, comparing the ratio C(Hα)/C(CO) between barred galaxies with AGNs and other galaxies.
AI.result: Four barred spiral galaxies with AGNs show C(Hα)/C(CO) ratios of ~0.3-0.4, while the other 13 galaxies show ratios ~1 (0.7-1.3). The low-ratio galaxies have molecular gas mass fractions < 0.1.
AI.conclusion: AGN feedback effectively suppresses star formation in barred galaxies with low molecular gas fractions, even when AGN activity is weak. Bar-driven gas inflow triggers starbursts, then AGN feedback rapidly quenches remaining gas, leading to faster quenching in AGN-barred galaxies. This unique quenching mechanism is essential for understanding galaxy evolution.

title: A No-Go Theorem for the Mass-Radius Relation of Solitons
comment: 6 pages, 1 figure
summary: We prove a no-go theorem for the mass-radius relation of localized and stable field configurations, known as solitons. Defining the mass-radius index by $Γ\equiv \frac{\rm{d}\ln M}{\rm{d}\ln R}$, for real scalar field theories in $d$ spatial dimensions, we show that typical non-topological, non-relativistic, and spherically symmetric solitons cannot have $Γ$ in the range $[0, d]$. The forces considered originate from gradient energy, self-interaction, and gravitation, with the typicality assumption excluding the fine-tuned region of the parameter space where all three forces have comparable strength. Importantly, the theorem works for an arbitrary self-interaction that, in the relativistic theory, is allowed to be non-power-law in the field, be non-analytic around the classical vacuum (where the field amplitude vanishes), or to include derivative couplings. Additionally, the theorem makes no assumptions about the explicit form of the soliton's density profile or the behavior of $Γ$ as a function of $R$. We also argue that the same exclusion applies to compact objects formed from self-gravitating, non-relativistic, barotropic fluids with arbitrary equations of state. As a consequence for cosmology, it is worth noting that observations favor a core in the centers of dark matter halos with $Γ\simeq 1.7$, which (for $d=3$) lies approximately in the middle of the excluded range. Therefore, proposals such as ultra-light or fluid-like dark matter models are essentially ruled out as natural explanations for halo cores, provided other astrophysical effects are negligible.

AI.tldr: The paper proves a no-go theorem stating that typical non-topological, non-relativistic, spherically symmetric solitons in d spatial dimensions cannot have a mass-radius index Γ in [0, d], ruling out many dark matter models that predict halo cores with Γ≈1.7 (for d=3) as natural explanations.
AI.motivation: To establish a rigorous no-go theorem constraining the mass-radius relation of solitons (localized stable field configurations), and to use this to assess the viability of dark matter models (e.g., ultra-light or fluid-like dark matter) that predict cored density profiles in galactic halos.
AI.method: The authors analyze the scaling behavior of soliton solutions under spatial rescaling, considering gradient energy, self-interaction, and gravitational forces. They impose a "typicality" assumption — excluding fine-tuned regions where all three forces are comparable — and prove the theorem for general (non-power-law, non-analytic, derivative-coupled) self-interactions without assuming specific density profiles.
AI.result: The mass-radius index Γ ≡ d ln M / d ln R cannot lie in the range [0, d] for typical non-topological, non-relativistic, spherically symmetric solitons. The same exclusion applies to self-gravitating barotropic fluids. Observational data favors Γ≈1.7 (for d=3), which falls within the excluded range.
AI.conclusion: Ultra-light or fluid-like dark matter models that predict cored halo profiles are essentially ruled out as natural explanations (absent fine-tuning or additional astrophysical effects), since their predicted Γ≈1.7 lies in the forbidden interval.

title: Rotation-curve residuals reveal a suppressed acceleration branch in dwarf galaxies
comment: 4 pages. 3 figures
summary: Galaxy rotation curves exhibit systematic deviations from the Newtonian expectation inferred from visible matter alone. Existing phenomenological descriptions capture many aspects of these deviations, but a common residual structure across massive disks and dwarf irregular galaxies remains unclear. We investigate whether rotation-curve residuals organize into a simple empirical form across the SPARC and LITTLE THINGS samples. We analyze 175 SPARC galaxies and 22 LITTLE THINGS dwarf irregular galaxies in velocity-squared space after subtracting a leading Newtonian-like term. We fit a generalized residual family, v^2-A/r=B+Cr^{q+1}, and examine which radial scaling is selected by the data. The galaxy population systematically favors the limit \(q\simeq0\), corresponding to an approximately linear residual relation, \(v^2-A/r=B+Cr\). SPARC galaxies generally occupy a high-\(B\) branch, whereas LITTLE THINGS dwarf galaxies show suppressed residual intercepts, including several systems consistent with \(B=0\). For the SPARC sample, the high-\(B\) branch approximately follows \(B\propto M_{\rm bar}^{0.72}\). {Rotation-curve residuals are not featureless scatter beyond the leading Newtonian-like contribution, but instead show a simple population-dependent empirical organization across massive and dwarf galaxy systems.}

AI.tldr: Analysis of 175 SPARC and 22 LITTLE THINGS galaxies reveals that rotation-curve residuals follow a simple empirical form, v² - A/r = B + Cr, with dwarf galaxies showing suppressed intercepts (B≈0) while SPARC galaxies exhibit a high-B branch scaling as B ∝ M_bar^0.72.
AI.motivation: Galaxy rotation curves deviate systematically from Newtonian predictions based on visible matter alone, and existing phenomenological descriptions leave unclear whether a common residual structure exists across both massive disks and dwarf irregular galaxies.
AI.method: Analyzed 175 SPARC and 22 LITTLE THINGS dwarf irregular galaxies in velocity-squared space after subtracting a leading Newtonian-like term. Fitted a generalized residual family v² - A/r = B + Cr^{q+1} and examined which radial scaling is favored by the data.
AI.result: The galaxy population systematically favors q≈0 (linear residual relation, v² - A/r = B + Cr). SPARC galaxies occupy a high-B branch (B ∝ M_bar^0.72), while LITTLE THINGS dwarfs show suppressed intercepts with several consistent with B=0.
AI.conclusion: Rotation-curve residuals are not featureless scatter but exhibit a simple population-dependent empirical organization across massive and dwarf galaxy systems.

title: The $τ$ of Neutral Hydrogen: Increased CMB Optical Depth at Long Wavelengths
comment: 10 pages, 4 figures
summary: At wavelengths longer than 21 cm, photons from the long-wavelength tail of the cosmic microwave background (CMB) have a non-zero probability of being absorbed by distant neutral hydrogen. This provides an additional suppression of the observed CMB clustering in addition to the usual Thomson scattering. The optical depth as a function of frequency is sensitive to the 21 cm spin temperature $T_s$ of the gas as a function of cosmic time, with the excess optical depth peaking at a level of a few percent around 100 MHz. The details depend on the specifics of the heating of cosmic gas and the evolution of the neutral fraction $x_{HI}$. It is likely difficult to detect the CMB at these long radio wavelengths, but the cause is aided by the ability to cross-correlate with the already well-characterized fluctuations at cm/mm frequencies. We find that detecting CMB fluctuations at radio wavelengths corresponding to the 21 cm ``dark ages'' in cross-correlation with mm-wave maps may be easier than detecting the intrinsic 21 cm fluctuations. Measurement of the amplitude of CMB fluctuations as a function of radio wavelength provides a path for a new type of direct measurement of the combination $x_{HI}/T_s$ as a function of redshift.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes that CMB photons at wavelengths >21 cm can be absorbed by neutral hydrogen, creating an additional suppression of CMB clustering. This effect depends on the 21 cm spin temperature and neutral fraction, and cross-correlating long-wavelength radio CMB maps with mm-wave CMB maps may be easier than detecting intrinsic 21 cm signals, offering a new way to measure x_HI/T_s across redshift.
AI.motivation: To explore a previously overlooked absorption mechanism of CMB photons by neutral hydrogen at long radio wavelengths (>21 cm) and assess its detectability for probing cosmic gas properties.
AI.method: The authors calculate the frequency-dependent optical depth from 21 cm absorption of the CMB tail, model its dependence on spin temperature T_s and neutral fraction x_HI, and propose cross-correlation between long-wavelength radio CMB maps and existing mm-wave CMB maps as a detection strategy.
AI.result: The excess optical depth peaks at ~a few percent around 100 MHz. Cross-correlation with mm-wave maps may be easier to detect than intrinsic 21 cm fluctuations.
AI.conclusion: Measuring CMB fluctuations as a function of radio wavelength enables a new type of direct measurement of x_HI/T_s as a function of redshift.

title: The dual effect of group-scale environments on galaxy quenching during cluster infall: pre-processing and protection
comment: 11 pages, 8 figures, accepted by A&A
summary: Context. It is well established that the cluster environment effectively quenches star formation in member galaxies. Amis. We aim to explore how the accretion path of infalling galaxies influences the cluster-driven quenching process. Methods. We compiled a large spectroscopic galaxy sample around 25 low-redshift, X-ray luminous massive clusters. We identified cluster substructures using the Blooming Tree algorithm and distinguished between galaxies accreted as part of group-scale structures and those accreted in isolation. The infall process was quantified using an infall proxy, $d_{\rm R}$, defined in the $R$--$V$ diagram. Results. Along the infall process, the quiescent fraction remains approximately constant at the outskirts and then increases steadily toward cluster center, with a transition occurring around $d_{\rm R}\sim 2.5$. We find that group-associated galaxies follow a distinct quenching track compared to isolated galaxies, indicating a dual effect of group-scale environments. At the early infall stages, group galaxies exhibit a higher quiescent fraction, consistent with ``pre-processing'' in group-scale halos. However, after entering the cluster environment, the rise in their quiescent fraction is delayed to smaller $d_{\rm R}$ compared to isolated galaxies. This suggests a phenomenological ``protection'' effect, in which group-scale halos buffer member galaxies against rapid cluster-driven quenching. Conclusions. We conclude that group-scale environments affect quenching in two ways: via pre-processing prior to cluster infall, and through a subsequent protection effect within the cluster environment.

AI.tldr: This study of 25 massive clusters shows that group-accreted galaxies experience a dual effect: pre-processing (higher quiescence before infall) and a protection effect (delayed quenching after entering the cluster), compared to galaxies accreted in isolation.
AI.motivation: To explore how the accretion path (group-scale vs. isolated infall) influences the cluster-driven quenching process in member galaxies.
AI.method: Compiled a spectroscopic galaxy sample around 25 low-redshift, X-ray luminous massive clusters; identified substructures with the Blooming Tree algorithm; distinguished group-accreted from isolated-accreted galaxies; quantified infall using the proxy $d_{\rm R}$ in the $R$--$V$ diagram.
AI.result: Quiescent fraction remains constant at outskirts then rises toward center, transitioning at $d_{\rm R}\sim 2.5$. Group galaxies show higher quiescent fraction at early infall (pre-processing) but delayed rise in quiescent fraction after entering the cluster (protection effect) compared to isolated galaxies.
AI.conclusion: Group-scale environments affect quenching in two ways: pre-processing prior to cluster infall and a protection effect within the cluster that buffers against rapid quenching.

title: Gravitational waves from cosmic strings with friction: analytical approximations and parameter space
comment: 16 pages, 10 figures; submitted to PRD
summary: We derive analytical approximations to describe the ultra-high-frequency secondary peak of the stochastic gravitational wave background generated by cosmic strings that is sourced by loops created in the friction-dominated era. We show that these approximations provide a very good description of the contribution of the friction-era loops over the relevant frequency range and for a broad range of cosmic string parameters, thus enabling a fast and accurate characterization of this signature. We also use these approximations to uncover the full parameter range in which this ultra-high-frequency peak should be distinguishable on the stochastic gravitational wave background spectrum and show that it should be present in a broader range of high-energy physics scenarios than originally reported in~\cite{Mukovnikov:2024zed}.

AI.tldr: The paper derives analytical approximations for the ultra-high-frequency secondary peak in the stochastic gravitational wave background from cosmic strings, specifically from loops formed during the friction-dominated era. These approximations accurately describe the signature across relevant frequencies and parameters, enabling fast characterization. The authors also identify a broader range of high-energy physics scenarios where this peak is distinguishable than previously reported.
AI.motivation: To enable fast and accurate characterization of the ultra-high-frequency secondary peak in the stochastic gravitational wave background from cosmic string loops created in the friction-dominated era, and to explore the full parameter space where this signature is distinguishable.
AI.method: Derivation of analytical approximations for the gravitational wave contribution of friction-era loops, validated against numerical results across a broad range of cosmic string parameters.
AI.result: The analytical approximations provide a very good description of the friction-era loop contribution over the relevant frequency range and parameter space. The ultra-high-frequency peak is distinguishable in a broader range of high-energy physics scenarios than previously reported.
AI.conclusion: The analytical approximations enable efficient and accurate characterization of this signature, and the parameter range where the peak is observable is larger than earlier work suggested.

title: Performance analysis of extragalactic classifications in Gaia Data Release 4
comment: Accepted by Astronomy and Astrophysics. 25 pages
summary: The Discrete Source Classifier (DSC) provides probabilistic classifications of sources in Gaia Data Release 4 (GDR4) based on empirically-trained Bayesian classifiers. Using Gaia astrometry, photometry, and low-resolution spectra (XP), DSC classifies all sources as quasars, galaxies, or stars. DSC comprises three trained neural networks and three combinations of their probabilities. When evaluated as a function of brightness and sky position on a test set excluding the Magellanic Clouds, the DSC purity in GDR4 has improved for a small loss in completeness. The average performance of the best classifiers at magnitudes brighter than G=20 is at least 88% completeness and 96% purity for the extragalactic classes, namely the quasar and galaxy classes. At fainter magnitudes, performance is lower due to increased noise. The average performance at magnitudes of 20$\leq$G<20.5 is a minimum of 55% completeness and 71% purity for the extragalactic classes. At G>20.5 mag, completeness is considerably reduced, primarily for the models that depend on the XP spectra. Furthermore, we train additional models on Gaia optical data together with mid-infrared photometry from the CatWISE2020 catalogue. Inclusion of infrared photometry increases the completeness of extragalactic samples at G>20 mag between 9 and 29 percentage points, at the cost of reducing purity between 1 and 9 percentage points. In GDR4, the best DSC-combined classifier prioritising completeness identifies three million quasars and two million galaxies, but with expected high contamination among fainter sources. In contrast, the combined classifiers prioritising purity identify approximately two million quasars and 1.3 million galaxies with an expected lower level of contamination. Finally, we provide recommendations for enhancing the purity of the DSC extragalactic selection by applying quality cuts to the Gaia photometry and astrometry.

AI.tldr: The Discrete Source Classifier (DSC) for Gaia DR4 uses Bayesian neural networks to classify sources as quasars, galaxies, or stars using Gaia astrometry, photometry, and XP spectra, with improved purity over previous releases. Best classifiers achieve ≥88% completeness and ≥96% purity for extragalactic sources at G<20, dropping to 55%/71% at G 20-20.5. Adding CatWISE2020 infrared data boosts completeness by 9-29 percentage points at G>20 with a 1-9 percentage point purity trade-off. The completeness-prioritized combined classifier identifies ~3M quasars and ~2M galaxies; the purity-prioritized one identifies ~2M quasars and ~1.3M galaxies.
AI.motivation: To provide probabilistic classifications of astronomical sources (quasars, galaxies, stars) in Gaia DR4 using empirically-trained Bayesian classifiers, enabling large-scale statistical studies of extragalactic populations while assessing classification performance across magnitude ranges and sky positions.
AI.method: Three trained neural networks and three combinations of their probabilities, using Gaia astrometry, photometry, and low-resolution XP spectra. Additional models incorporate mid-infrared photometry from CatWISE2020. Quality cuts on Gaia photometry and astrometry are recommended to enhance purity.
AI.result: At G<20: ≥88% completeness, ≥96% purity for extragalactic classes. At 20≤G<20.5: ≥55% completeness, ≥71% purity. At G>20.5: completeness significantly reduced, especially for XP-dependent models. Adding IR photometry increases completeness by 9-29 pp but reduces purity by 1-9 pp at G>20. Completeness-prioritized classifier: ~3M quasars, ~2M galaxies. Purity-prioritized classifier: ~2M quasars, ~1.3M galaxies.
AI.conclusion: DSC in GDR4 shows improved purity over prior releases with some completeness loss. Performance degrades at fainter magnitudes. Infrared data improves faint-source completeness at a modest purity cost. Quality cuts on photometry/astrometry are recommended to further enhance purity of extragalactic selections.

title: Increasing the Precision of Surrogate Models for Weak Lensing Mass Maps with Flow Matching
summary: Weak gravitational lensing maps compactly encode the evolution of cosmic large-scale structure and are a key tool for cosmological analyses. Performing inference directly at the map level allows flexible choices of statistics and can increase constraining power. Conventional methods rely solely on N-body simulations and are computationally expensive. Generative machine-learning emulators can accelerate map-level theory prediction. However, existing GAN-based map-level surrogates still have limited statistical fidelity. They can produce over-smoothed maps, may fail to capture the full distribution of generated map sets and can be difficult to train. Continuous normalizing flows trained with flow matching have recently emerged as a powerful class of generative models. We present a residual label-conditional flow matching generative network that conditions explicitly on the matter density Omega_m and clustering amplitude sigma_8 for a fixed source redshift distribution n(z). The model learns a continuous probability flow in a residual space from label-specific noise distributions to convergence maps. We evaluate it using pixel and peak statistics, the power spectrum, bispectrum, power-spectrum correlation matrices, and other validation metrics. Compared with the previous GAN benchmark, the proposed method improves the typical fidelity of generated maps from below 10% and below 20% to below 1% and below 5% for basic and higher-order statistics, respectively. The agreement at the level of map distributions is also very good: maps generated from random noise match well the distribution of maps generated with N-body simulations from random initial conditions. This work brings us closer to a practical mass-map emulator that captures the cosmological signal while supporting multiple forms of data analysis.

AI.tldr: A residual label-conditional flow matching generative network is proposed for weak gravitational lensing convergence map emulation, achieving sub-1% and sub-5% fidelity for basic and higher-order statistics, significantly outperforming previous GAN-based methods.
AI.motivation: Map-level inference for weak gravitational lensing is powerful but computationally expensive when relying solely on N-body simulations. Existing GAN-based generative emulators suffer from limited statistical fidelity, over-smoothed maps, and training difficulties.
AI.method: A residual label-conditional continuous normalizing flow trained with flow matching, conditioned on Omega_m and sigma_8 for fixed source redshift distribution n(z). The model learns a continuous probability flow in a residual space from label-specific noise to convergence maps.
AI.result: Improves fidelity from below 10% (basic stats) and below 20% (higher-order stats) with GANs to below 1% and below 5% respectively. Maps generated from random noise match well with N-body simulation distributions.
AI.conclusion: This work advances toward a practical mass-map emulator that captures cosmological signals and supports multiple forms of data analysis.

title: ALMA CO-CAVITY I. Resolved Molecular Gas in Void Galaxies
comment: 20 pages, 12 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: The environment plays a key role in galaxy evolution, yet it remains unclear how detailed molecular gas properties and their connection to star formation and stellar content are influenced by both large-scale and local environments. Here we introduce the ALMA CO-CAVITY project, the first interferometric CO(1-0) survey of a large sample of 41 void galaxies (VGs) to characterise in detail their molecular gas properties. It is built over the CAVITY project, offering optical integral field unit (IFU) data, enabling a direct, pixel-to-pixel comparison between molecular gas (from ALMA), star formation, and stellar properties, as well as the derivation of their scaling relations. In this work we present ALMA data products for our sample, containing data cubes, moment maps and position-velocity diagrams at angular resolutions of 1 arcsec. We also present molecular gas, stellar mass, and star formation rate surface density maps at a common resolution of 2.5 arcsec. We contextualise our sample against representative unresolved and resolved surveys. While our sample provides a good representation of the VG population and follows the distribution of key properties seen in star-forming galaxy samples, galaxies included in resolved studies from the literature tend to be more massive, less isolated, and located in denser large-scale environments. We present global scaling relations for the ALMA CO-CAVITY sample and find that the molecular gas main sequence exhibits the smallest scatter (0.21 dex), followed by the Schmidt-Kennicutt relation and the star-forming main sequence. From integrated properties alone, we find that these scaling relations for VGs are compatible with those for denser environments. This paper lays the foundation for forthcoming studies exploiting this unique dataset.

AI.tldr: The ALMA CO-CAVITY project presents the first interferometric CO(1-0) survey of 41 void galaxies, combining ALMA molecular gas data with optical IFU observations to enable pixel-to-pixel comparisons. The paper provides data products (cubes, moment maps, PV diagrams at 1″ resolution) and surface density maps at 2.5″ resolution. Voids galaxies follow standard star-forming scaling relations with the molecular gas main sequence showing the smallest scatter (0.21 dex), and their integrated relations are compatible with galaxies in denser environments.
AI.motivation: To understand how molecular gas properties and their connection to star formation and stellar content are influenced by both large-scale (void vs. denser) and local environments, a question that remains unclear despite the recognized role of environment in galaxy evolution.
AI.method: ALMA interferometric CO(1-0) observations of 41 void galaxies from the CAVITY project, combined with optical IFU data for pixel-to-pixel comparisons. Data products include cubes, moment maps, PV diagrams (1″ resolution) and surface density maps (2.5″ resolution). Sample contextualized against representative unresolved and resolved surveys.
AI.result: The sample represents the VG population well. VGs follow key star-forming galaxy distributions. The molecular gas main sequence has the smallest scatter (0.21 dex), followed by the Schmidt-Kennicutt relation and the star-forming main sequence. Integrated scaling relations for VGs are compatible with those in denser environments.
AI.conclusion: This paper provides the foundational dataset and first scaling relations for the ALMA CO-CAVITY project, establishing that void galaxies are compatible with galaxies in denser environments in terms of global scaling relations, while noting that resolved literature samples tend to be more massive, less isolated, and in denser environments.

title: Dissecting the Perseus-Pisces supercluster observed with CFHT-MegaCam: Exploring late-type galaxy shape alignments within the local cosmic web
comment: 14 pages, 12 figures
summary: Intrinsic alignments of galaxy shapes are a major systematic for weak gravitational lensing and provide insight into how galaxies acquire orientations within the cosmic web. Most studies rely on large statistical samples; here, we probe this signal in a single nearby superstructure, extending to outer regions where secondary infall should dominate. We measure intrinsic alignments in the Perseus-Pisces supercluster as a function of galaxy morphology and radial extent into the low surface brightness regime. Using deep CFHT r-band imaging covering 367 deg2 (mainly from the UNIONS survey) and reaching 28 mag/arcsec2, we compute correlation functions at three isophotal radii for 2004 galaxies with log M*/Msun > 8.6, stratified by morphology and stellar mass in comoving coordinates. We detect positive intrinsic alignment signals for both early- and late-type galaxies out to 1 Mpc/h, including a clear signal for spirals. Shape-shape correlations are stronger than position-shape correlations, while comoving measurements increase the fraction of strongly correlated systems. Correlation profiles show little radial dependence across the three isophotes despite ellipticity variations in 10-20% of galaxies. We find strong morphology dependence: late-type galaxies dominate the shape-shape signal, preferentially inhabiting filaments and displaying higher ellipticities consistent with edge-on orientations. Early-type galaxies instead cluster near group and cluster centers, with no comparable excess in position-shape correlations. This segregation suggests distinct alignment mechanisms: tidal stretching for early-types in dense environments and tidal torquing for late-types in filaments. These local-Universe constraints inform intrinsic alignment modeling for Euclid, DESI, and LSST, highlighting the contribution of blue spiral galaxies to low-redshift cosmic shear contamination.

AI.tldr: This paper measures intrinsic galaxy shape alignments in the Perseus-Pisces supercluster using deep CFHT imaging, finding positive alignment signals for both early- and late-type galaxies out to 1 Mpc/h, with morphology-dependent alignment mechanisms: tidal stretching for early-types in dense environments and tidal torquing for late-types in filaments, informing IA models for upcoming surveys.
AI.motivation: Intrinsic alignments (IA) of galaxy shapes are a major systematic for weak gravitational lensing and provide insight into how galaxies acquire orientations within the cosmic web. Most studies rely on large statistical samples; this work probes this signal in a single nearby superstructure, extending to outer regions where secondary infall should dominate.
AI.method: Using deep CFHT r-band imaging covering 367 deg² (mainly from UNIONS survey) reaching 28 mag/arcsec², the authors compute correlation functions at three isophotal radii for 2004 galaxies with log M*/M⊙ > 8.6, stratified by morphology and stellar mass in comoving coordinates within the Perseus-Pisces supercluster.
AI.result: Positive IA signals detected for both early- and late-type galaxies out to 1 Mpc/h, including a clear signal for spirals. Shape-shape correlations are stronger than position-shape correlations. Late-type galaxies dominate the shape-shape signal with higher ellipticities consistent with edge-on orientations in filaments. Early-type galaxies cluster near group/ cluster centers with no comparable excess in position-shape correlations.
AI.conclusion: The observed morphology-dependent segregation suggests distinct alignment mechanisms: tidal stretching for early-types in dense environments and tidal torquing for late-types in filaments. These local-Universe constraints inform IA modeling for Euclid, DESI, and LSST, highlighting the contribution of blue spiral galaxies to low-redshift cosmic shear contamination.

title: Insights from Analytical Theory of Eccentric Circumbinary Disks II. Forced Modes and Resonance for Precessing Binaries
summary: An eccentric, unequal-mass binary induces forced eccentricity in a circumbinary disk through the non-axisymmetric component of its gravitational potential. Building on the theory of free (i.e., unforced) eccentric modes, we develop a semi-analytical framework to describe this response in two-dimensional, locally isothermal disks with a power-law surface density profile. We show that the disk eccentricity is governed by the competition between pressure and the binary quadrupole potential, leading to two distinct regimes. In quadrupole-dominated disks, the eccentricity oscillates about the forced eccentricity of a test particle, $E\sim r^{-1}$, with an amplitude and wavelength set by the disk aspect ratio. In pressure-dominated disks, the eccentricity departs qualitatively from the test-particle limit and follows a universal radial scaling $E\sim r^{-2}$, consistent with recent numerical results. Resonant amplification occurs when the binary forcing frequency matches the eigenfrequency of a free eccentric disk mode. In the limit of a non-precessing binary, this reduces to the previously identified zero-frequency resonance, for which we derive an analytic criterion and map its dependence on disk and binary parameters. We extend the framework to massive disks by including the disk's gravitational potential and allowing binary apsidal precession. We conjecture that the cavity size, for eccentric, non-equal-mass binaries, can be set such that the ground free eccentric mode of the disk has an eigenfrequency equal to the binary precession frequency. In other words, the disk cavity adjusts until the lowest-order trapped eccentric mode resonates with the forcing from the precessing binary.

AI.tldr: This paper develops a semi-analytical framework for forced eccentricity in circumbinary disks around eccentric, unequal-mass binaries, identifying two regimes (quadrupole- vs. pressure-dominated), deriving scaling laws, resonant conditions, and a cavity-size conjecture based on mode locking with binary precession.
AI.motivation: To understand how non-axisymmetric gravitational potential from eccentric, unequal-mass binaries drives forced eccentricity in circumbinary disks, extending prior free eccentric mode theory to the forced case.
AI.method: Semi-analytical framework for 2D locally isothermal disks with power-law surface density; analysis of competition between pressure and binary quadrupole potential; extension to massive disks including self-gravity and binary precession.
AI.result: Two regimes identified: quadrupole-dominated disks show eccentricity oscillating about $E\sim r^{-1}$; pressure-dominated disks show $E\sim r^{-2}$. Resonant amplification occurs when binary forcing frequency matches free eccentric mode eigenfrequency. Analytic criterion for zero-frequency resonance derived.
AI.conclusion: The disk cavity size may be set so that the ground free eccentric mode resonates with the binary precession frequency, i.e., the cavity adjusts to trap the lowest-order eccentric mode in resonance with the forcing.

title: Cosmological constraints from neighbor-density-weighted marked correlation functions
comment: 16 pages, 13 figures
summary: We investigate whether neighbor-density-weighted marked correlation functions (MCFs) can extract cosmological information beyond the standard redshift-space two-point correlation function (2PCF). Using the Kun suite of 129 $w_0w_a$CDM$+\sum m_ν$ simulations in $1~h^{-1}{\rm Gpc}$ boxes, we construct Gaussian-process emulators for the normalized scale statistic $\widehat{W}^α(s)$ and the angular statistic $\widehat{W}^α_{Δs}(μ)$. We perform joint analyses combining multiple mark parameters $α$ and quantify the information gain using the FoM in the $Ω_m$--$σ_8$ plane. Relative to the 2PCF case, three-mark combinations improve the FoM by factors of $1.7$--$2.5$, while five-mark combinations increase the gain to $1.9$--$2.4$, depending on the statistic and mark definition. We further compare density and normalized-gradient marks, finding that they are nearly redundant for isotropic statistics but complementary for angular statistics, where their combination improves the FoM by up to $43\%$. Tests of scale range and halo selection show that the marked statistics remain robust under changes in analysis choices, with the angular statistic retaining additional cosmological information that is less sensitive to tracer selection. Our results demonstrate that MCFs substantially enhance cosmological constraints beyond the standard 2PCF and provide a robust probe for next-generation galaxy surveys.

AI.tldr: Marked correlation functions (MCFs) with neighbor-density weighting extract cosmological information beyond the standard 2PCF, improving the figure of merit in the Ωm–σ8 plane by factors of 1.7–2.5 with three-mark combinations and 1.9–2.4 with five-mark combinations, based on Gaussian-process emulators built from 129 w0waCDM+∑mν simulations.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether neighbor-density-weighted marked correlation functions can extract cosmological information beyond what is available from the standard redshift-space two-point correlation function alone.
AI.method: Used 129 w0waCDM+∑mν simulations (Kun suite) in 1 h⁻¹Gpc boxes; constructed Gaussian-process emulators for normalized scale statistic Ŵ^α(s) and angular statistic Ŵ^α_{Δs}(μ); performed joint analyses combining multiple mark parameters α; quantified information gain via FoM in the Ωm–σ8 plane.
AI.result: Three-mark combinations improve FoM by factors of 1.7–2.5; five-mark combinations improve FoM by 1.9–2.4 relative to 2PCF. Density and normalized-gradient marks are nearly redundant for isotropic statistics but complementary for angular statistics (up to 43% FoM improvement). Marked statistics remain robust under changes in scale range and halo selection.
AI.conclusion: MCFs substantially enhance cosmological constraints beyond the standard 2PCF and provide a robust probe for next-generation galaxy surveys.

title: Cosmic web stripping and starvation of low-mass filament galaxies in TNG50
comment: 12 pages
summary: Galaxy properties are known to correlate with their location within the cosmic web. However, the role of filaments remains poorly understood, particularly for low-mass galaxies, which are expected to be more sensitive to environmental effects. In this work, we use the TNG50-1 simulation to investigate the properties of low-mass $8 \le \log(M_{star}/M_{sun}) \le 10$ galaxies in filaments and in the field, when controlling for stellar and halo mass and excluding the role of groups and clusters. We find that their integrated properties, including stellar, halo mass assembly and quenched fractions, are similar between the two environments. However, we demonstrate that filament galaxies exhibit smaller and more asymmetric cold gas discs with respect to their field counterparts. We identify two main mechanisms driving these differences. For galaxies that entered filaments in the early Universe, during the phase of active accretion, cosmic web tidal fields modify the accretion of gas and dark matter. In some systems, accretion proceeds at rates comparable to the field but with a different geometry, leading to more tangential motions in the dark matter halo and, consequently, smaller gas discs. In others, the tidal field significantly suppresses both gas and dark matter accretion, leading to a starvation-like evolution, in which galaxies gradually exhaust their gas through star formation and can eventually quench. In contrast, galaxies that fall into filaments at late times can undergo cosmic web stripping, a rapid hydrodynamical removal of gas analogous to ram-pressure stripping in clusters. Our results suggest that spatially resolved gas properties are sensitive to several filament-driven environmental mechanisms.

AI.tldr: Using TNG50-1 simulations, this study finds that low-mass galaxies ($8 \le \log(M_{star}/M_{sun}) \le 10$) in filaments and the field have similar integrated properties (stellar mass, halo mass assembly, quenched fractions) when controlling for mass and excluding groups/clusters, but filament galaxies have smaller and more asymmetric cold gas discs due to two mechanisms: early cosmic web tidal fields altering accretion geometry/suppressing accretion, and late-time cosmic web stripping (ram-pressure-like gas removal).
AI.motivation: Galaxy properties correlate with cosmic web location, but the role of filaments, especially for low-mass galaxies expected to be more environmentally sensitive, remains poorly understood.
AI.method: The authors use the TNG50-1 simulation to compare low-mass galaxies ($8 \le \log(M_{star}/M_{sun}) \le 10$) in filaments versus the field, controlling for stellar and halo mass and excluding groups/clusters.
AI.result: Integrated properties (stellar/halo mass assembly, quenched fractions) are similar between filament and field galaxies. However, filament galaxies have smaller and more asymmetric cold gas discs. Two mechanisms drive these differences: (1) early entry into filaments leads to cosmic web tidal fields that modify accretion geometry (more tangential motions, smaller gas discs) or suppress accretion (starvation-like evolution); (2) late-time filament entry leads to cosmic web stripping (rapid hydrodynamical gas removal analogous to ram-pressure stripping).
AI.conclusion: Spatially resolved gas properties are sensitive to several filament-driven environmental mechanisms, even when integrated properties appear indistinguishable from the field.

title: Scalable Dark Siren Cosmology with gwcosmo: GPU Acceleration, Validation and Systematics
summary: As the number of confident gravitational-wave detections grows, population-level hierarchical analyses face increasing computational costs. Dark-siren cosmological inference integrates over the localisation volume of each gravitational-wave source. To remain feasible without discarding information from the quieter but more numerous sources in the catalogue, significant efficiency improvements are vital for analysis pipelines. In this work, we present an upgraded version of the cosmological inference pipeline gwcosmo, which leverages vectorisation on graphics processing units to process the entire gravitational-wave catalogue in parallel with each iteration. This new implementation achieves a speed-up of 1000 times over the previous version, facilitating analyses of O5-like numbers of GW events on wall-clock timescales of hours. Our results demonstrate the scalability of the gwcosmo pipeline, specifically its ability to handle the increasing computational load of expanding event catalogues, positioning it as a vital tool for future advances in dark-siren cosmology.

AI.tldr: The paper presents an upgraded version of the gwcosmo pipeline that uses GPU vectorisation to process gravitational-wave catalogues in parallel, achieving a 1000x speed-up over the previous version and enabling analyses of O5-scale events in hours.
AI.motivation: As confident gravitational-wave detections increase, population-level hierarchical analyses face growing computational costs. Dark-siren cosmological inference must integrate over the localisation volume of each source, and without significant efficiency improvements, it becomes infeasible to process quieter but more numerous sources in expanding catalogues.
AI.method: The upgraded gwcosmo pipeline leverages vectorisation on graphics processing units (GPUs) to process the entire gravitational-wave catalogue in parallel with each iteration.
AI.result: The new implementation achieves a 1000-fold speed-up over the previous version, enabling analyses of O5-like numbers of GW events on wall-clock timescales of hours.
AI.conclusion: The gwcosmo pipeline demonstrates scalability to handle increasing computational loads from expanding event catalogues, positioning it as a vital tool for future advances in dark-siren cosmology.

title: Disruption of a Giant: Spectroscopic Identification of Members in the Periphery and Tidal Tails of $ω$ Centauri
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures, submitted to MNRAS. Note: the data underlying this paper will become available after the paper is accepted for publication
summary: $ω$ Centauri ($ω$ Cen, NGC 5139) is one of the most enigmatic globular clusters in the Milky Way, with the recent detection of tidal tails adding further to its complexity. We report the results of a spectroscopic study of stars in the outer regions of $ω$ Cen, which provides an improved characterisation of the cluster periphery and confirms the existence of tidal tails. Our targets, which lie in six VLT/FLAMES fields sampling six degrees across the sky, are selected using the Bayesian inference technique of arXiv:2108.02531. We confirm 157 high-probability members of $ω$ Cen based on line-of-sight velocity and [Fe/H] measurements, indicating an overall success rate of 93 per cent. We trace stars along the tidal tails to a cluster-centric radius of 3.2~deg, identifying five high-probability members and additional lower-probability candidates. The analysis of the kinematics and metallicities of the new members provides evidence of continuity in these properties from the bound component of the progenitor cluster into its tidal debris. We find that the metallicities of stars in the peripheral regions and tidal tails of $ω$ Cen are broadly consistent with those in the \textit{Fimbulthul} stream to which the cluster has been previously linked. Our study provides a glimpse of the promise of new and forthcoming wide-field multi-object spectrographs for advancing understanding of tidal structures around Milky Way globular clusters.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a spectroscopic study of stars in the outer regions of ω Centauri, confirming the existence of tidal tails extending to a cluster-centric radius of 3.2° and identifying 157 high-probability members with 93% success rate. Kinematic and metallicity analyses show continuity from the bound cluster to its tidal debris, with metallicities consistent with the Fimbulthul stream.
AI.motivation: To improve characterisation of the periphery of ω Centauri and confirm the existence of its tidal tails, which add to the cluster's enigmatic nature and complexity.
AI.method: Spectroscopic study using VLT/FLAMES across six fields covering six degrees on the sky, with target selection via Bayesian inference (arXiv:2108.02531). Line-of-sight velocity and [Fe/H] measurements were used to confirm membership.
AI.result: 157 high-probability members confirmed (93% success rate). Tidal tails traced to 3.2°, with five high-probability and additional lower-probability members identified. Metallicities of peripheral and tidal tail stars are consistent with the Fimbulthul stream.
AI.conclusion: Kinematics and metallicity show continuity between the bound cluster and its tidal debris. The study demonstrates the potential of new wide-field multi-object spectrographs for studying tidal structures around Milky Way globular clusters.

title: cloelib: A Flexible Python Library for Computing Cosmological Observables in the Euclid Era
summary: cloelib is a Python library developed to compute cosmological observables within the Cosmology Likelihood for Observables in Euclid (CLOE) ecosystem (cloe-org). As cosmology enters a precision era driven by galaxy survey missions such as Euclid, there is a growing need for flexible, efficient, and differentiable software capable of supporting next-generation inference pipelines. cloelib addresses these demands through a modular architecture that interfaces seamlessly with established Boltzmann solvers whilst incorporating JAX-based automatic differentiation to enable gradient-based methods. The library defines consistent protocols for background evolution, perturbations, and non-linear structure formation, and supports a wide range of observables, including photometric and spectroscopic large-scale structure probes, as well as cross-correlations with the Cosmic Microwave Background and galaxy clusters. In its finalised form, cloelib is intended to serve as the reference theory computation infrastructure for Euclid's first cosmological release, bridging traditional numerical cosmology with modern optimisation techniques and emerging machine learning approaches to inference.

AI.tldr: cloelib is a Python library for computing cosmological observables within the CLOE ecosystem, featuring JAX-based automatic differentiation, modular architecture interfacing with Boltzmann solvers, and support for multiple observables including LSS probes and CMB cross-correlations, designed as the reference theory infrastructure for Euclid's first cosmological release.
AI.motivation: As cosmology enters a precision era driven by galaxy survey missions such as Euclid, there is a growing need for flexible, efficient, and differentiable software capable of supporting next-generation inference pipelines.
AI.method: cloelib employs a modular architecture interfacing with established Boltzmann solvers while incorporating JAX-based automatic differentiation for gradient-based methods. It defines consistent protocols for background evolution, perturbations, and non-linear structure formation, supporting photometric and spectroscopic LSS probes, CMB cross-correlations, and galaxy cluster observables.
AI.result: The library bridges traditional numerical cosmology with modern optimization techniques and emerging machine learning approaches to inference, and is intended to serve as the reference theory computation infrastructure for Euclid's first cosmological release.
AI.conclusion: cloelib addresses the demands of next-generation cosmological inference by combining flexible, differentiable computation with established Boltzmann solvers within a unified ecosystem, positioning itself as the standard theory infrastructure for Euclid.

title: A comparison between Galactic magnetic field models and polarized synchrotron emission with C-BASS at 4.76 GHz and S-PASS at 2.3 GHz
comment: accepted in MNRAS
summary: We compare a set of contemporary Galactic magnetic field (GMF) models with polarized synchrotron observations from the S-PASS and C-BASS radio surveys and combine them to create a reconstructed 4.76~GHz full sky map. Pixels that potentially have a large Faraday rotation are excluded while small ($< 80\degree$) Faraday corrections derived at the respective frequencies of the two surveys are applied to the rest of the map. Using a template-fitting approach, we evaluate the ability of each model to reproduce the observed polarization amplitudes and polarization angles. We find that while most GMF models match the polarization angles reasonably well, they often fail to reproduce the morphology of the polarized intensity. We find that for most models there is a clear correlation between the data and models in polarization angles on large scales, but this does not hold true for polarized intensity. Our results show that a large portion of the polarized sky is shaped by local ``foreground'' features such as the North Polar Spur/Loop\,I and the Fan region. We conclude that incorporating such local structures is essential for accurately modelling the polarized synchrotron emission at microwave frequencies.

AI.tldr: This paper compares contemporary Galactic magnetic field (GMF) models with polarized synchrotron observations from S-PASS and C-BASS surveys, creating a reconstructed 4.76 GHz full-sky map after Faraday corrections. Template-fitting shows most GMF models match polarization angles on large scales but fail to reproduce polarized intensity morphology. Local foreground features like the North Polar Spur/Loop I and Fan region dominate the polarized sky, and the authors conclude such local structures are essential for accurate modeling.
AI.motivation: To evaluate how well current GMF models reproduce observed polarized synchrotron emission and to identify key missing components in these models, particularly local foreground structures.
AI.method: Combined S-PASS and C-BASS survey data into a 4.76 GHz full-sky map; excluded pixels with large Faraday rotation; applied small Faraday corrections; used template-fitting to compare GMF models against observed polarization amplitudes and angles.
AI.result: Most GMF models match polarization angles reasonably well on large scales but systematically fail to reproduce polarized intensity morphology. Local foreground features (North Polar Spur/Loop I, Fan region) dominate the polarized sky.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating local foreground structures is essential for accurately modeling polarized synchrotron emission at microwave frequencies.

title: cloelike: A Python Library for Cosmological Likelihood Inference in the Euclid Era
summary: cloelike is a Python package providing modular, composable Gaussian likelihood classes for the main cosmological large-scale structure observables targeted by the ESA Euclid space mission. It is a core component of the CLOE (Cosmology Likelihood for Observables in Euclid) ecosystem and interfaces directly with cloelib for theoretical predictions and euclidlib for reading official Euclid data products. The package implements Gaussian likelihoods covering harmonic angular power spectra and real-space two-point correlation functions for weak lensing (WL), photometric galaxy clustering (GCph), and Galaxy-Galaxy Lensing (GGL) in all joint probe combinations (3x2pt, 2x2pt), as well as spectroscopic full-shape power spectrum multipoles, and baryonic Acoustic oscillations (BAO). cloelike is actively used in internal Euclid Consortium analyses and is openly released to support community validation and reproducibility.

AI.tldr: cloelike is an open-source Python package that provides Gaussian likelihood classes for cosmological analyses of Euclid mission observables, including weak lensing, galaxy clustering, galaxy-galaxy lensing, spectroscopic power spectra, and BAO, supporting joint probe combinations and interfacing with theoretical and data-handling libraries.
AI.motivation: To provide a modular, composable, and reproducible Gaussian likelihood framework for the main cosmological large-scale structure observables targeted by the ESA Euclid space mission, enabling community validation and reproducibility.
AI.method: The package implements Gaussian likelihoods for harmonic angular power spectra and real-space two-point correlation functions across WL, GCph, and GGL in joint probe combinations (3x2pt, 2x2pt), plus spectroscopic full-shape power spectrum multipoles and BAO, interfacing with cloelib for theory predictions and euclidlib for Euclid data products.
AI.result: cloelike is actively used in internal Euclid Consortium analyses and is openly released to support community validation and reproducibility.
AI.conclusion: The package provides a core, openly available likelihood component of the CLOE ecosystem for Euclid cosmology analyses, enabling joint probe combinations and facilitating reproducible scientific workflows.

title: Examining extinction distributions for type Ia supernovae in simulated 3D galaxies
comment: 13 pages, 7 figures, submitted for publication to A&A
summary: Dust extinction and reddening greatly contribute to type Ia supernovae (SNe Ia) observed color and magnitude variations. The models used to describe the extinction probability density function (PDF) are often simplistic, which can negatively impact SN simulations and cosmology. We present an analysis of simulated SN Ia extinction in galaxies along realistic lines of sight and investigate the parameterization of its PDF, as well as its dependence on host properties. We employed SKIRT, a radiative transfer code, to simulate observations of SNe Ia in different environments and generate synthetic extinction distributions. To parameterize and fit these distributions, we used both the commonly assumed single-parameter exponential PDF and some of its two-parameter generalizations. We find that the standard exponential PDF does not adequately describe simulated SN extinction: It underestimates low-extinction events and overestimates high-extinction ones. 2D KS tests show significant differences between the simulated extinction distributions for SNe in different environments, which the exponential parameterization cannot properly distinguish. In contrast, the two-parameter PDFs parameterize SN extinction distributions more accurately across all simulated environments. Variations in host morphology or dust mass relate to variations in different PDF parameters, meaning that the two effects can effectively be disentangled. We conclude that the two-parameter Weibull or exponentiated exponential PDFs offer the best parameterizations of SN Ia extinction for a wide range of simulated environments. Analyzing observed SN colors from the literature and assuming a Gaussian distribution for the intrinsic component, we conclude that a two-parameter extinction PDF results in intrinsically redder SNe, with their mean intrinsic color shifted ~2$σ$ in relation to the standard exponential extinction PDF.

AI.tldr: The standard single-parameter exponential PDF inadequately models SN Ia dust extinction, underestimating low-extinction and overestimating high-extinction events. Two-parameter PDFs (Weibull or exponentiated exponential) provide significantly better fits across diverse simulated environments, and adopting them shifts the inferred intrinsic color of SNe Ia toward redder values by ~2σ.
AI.motivation: Dust extinction and reddening are major contributors to observed color and magnitude variations in SNe Ia, but commonly used exponential extinction PDFs are too simplistic, negatively impacting SN simulations and cosmological parameter estimation.
AI.method: Used the SKIRT radiative transfer code to simulate SN Ia observations along realistic lines of sight in galaxies, generating synthetic extinction distributions. Compared the standard single-parameter exponential PDF against two-parameter generalizations (e.g., Weibull, exponentiated exponential) using 2D KS tests and fits across varying host properties (morphology, dust mass).
AI.result: The exponential PDF significantly underestimates low-extinction events and overestimates high-extinction ones. Two-parameter PDFs fit all simulated environments more accurately. Variations in host morphology and dust mass map to distinct PDF parameters, enabling disentanglement. Adopting a two-parameter PDF shifts the inferred mean intrinsic color of SNe Ia ~2σ redder compared to the exponential assumption.
AI.conclusion: Two-parameter Weibull or exponentiated exponential PDFs are the best parameterizations for SN Ia extinction across a wide range of environments, and their use has important implications for the inferred intrinsic colors of SNe Ia and for cosmological analyses.

title: Atomic gas properties at the positions of supernovae Type Ia, II, and Ib/c
summary: Understanding which stars explode as which type of supernovae (SNe) is crucial to measure their contribution to the metal production and feedback halting star formation. Most of the studies of the gas in the environment of SNe are limited by a small sample size ($<10$). The goal of this paper is to present the first analysis of atomic gas properties at the positions of a statistically significant sample of SNe in order to constrain their nature. We selected 133 SNe (29 Ia, 77 II, 27 Ib/c) which have exploded in galaxies with existing atomic gas data. In order to test whether SN positions trace enhancements in the atomic gas distribution, we analyzed the fraction of pixels on the {\hi} map which are fainter than the pixel in which SN is located and the fraction of the {\hi} flux contributed by these pixels. All types of SNe deviate from the completely random distribution. From the three types of SNe, Type II showed the largest offset from the {\hi} distribution, preferring even higher concentrations of atomic gas. This type of SNe deviated also from being proportional to the stellar surface density of the host. The results are, however, complicated by the limits of the survey in size, and in the un-even resolution of the {\hi} observations. Furthermore, by direct comparison between the three SN types, we observed that the distributions of these populations are still consistent with each other. The obtained results fail to ascertain that Ib/c core-collapse SNe, and possibly also Type II SNe, are connected with the densest concentrations of atomic gas in their hosts, unlike what has been suggested for GRBs and Ic-BL SNe. Hence, the birth of progenitors of Type II and Ib/c SNe is still consistent with being connected with the current star formation in their hosts, whereas the progenitors of GRBs and Type Ic-BL SNe require more special conditions to form, for example low metallicity.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes atomic gas properties at the positions of 133 supernovae (29 Ia, 77 II, 27 Ib/c) to constrain their progenitor nature. All SN types deviate from random distributions, with Type II showing the largest offset toward higher atomic gas concentrations. However, distributions across SN types remain statistically consistent, and core-collapse SNe (Ib/c, II) do not show a clear connection to the densest atomic gas concentrations, unlike GRBs and Ic-BL SNe.
AI.motivation: Understanding which stars explode as which type of supernovae is crucial for measuring their contribution to metal production and feedback halting star formation. Previous studies were limited by small sample sizes (<10), motivating the need for a statistically significant analysis.
AI.method: Selected 133 SNe (29 Ia, 77 II, 27 Ib/c) in galaxies with existing HI atomic gas data. Analyzed the fraction of pixels on HI maps fainter than the SN pixel and the fraction of HI flux contributed by those pixels, comparing SN positions to random distributions and stellar surface density.
AI.result: All SN types deviate from random HI distributions. Type II SNe show the largest offset toward higher atomic gas concentrations and deviate from being proportional to stellar surface density. However, distributions across the three types remain statistically consistent with each other. Results do not confirm that Ib/c or Type II SNe are connected to the densest atomic gas concentrations.
AI.conclusion: Progenitors of Type II and Ib/c SNe are consistent with being connected to current star formation in their hosts, whereas GRBs and Type Ic-BL SNe require more special conditions (e.g., low metallicity) to form. Results are complicated by survey size limits and uneven HI observation resolution.

title: Multi-layered model-based characterisation of the local-Universe galaxy data from the GAMA survey
comment: 14 pages, 9 files, 4 tables; accepted for publication in the Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society
summary: Understanding the formation and evolution of galaxy populations requires robust classification and characterisation techniques that jointly account for internal galaxy properties and environment. We analyse $5,306$ galaxies from the Galaxy And Mass Assembly (GAMA) survey, described by stellar mass, specific star formation rate, $u-r$ colour, half-light radius, Sérsic index, and a combined environmental measure given by the optimal density. Unlike distance-based unsupervised clustering methods, our framework provides a probabilistic characterisation of galaxy populations, accommodates heavy-tailed feature distributions, and captures dependence among observables through latent factors. We model the sample using a $t$-mixture of factor analysers with group-specific latent structures (M$t$FAD), and then apply model-estimated overlap-based syncytial clustering (MOBSynC) to merge weakly separated groups and recover higher-level population structure. The first stage identifies eight simple clusters. The third and the fourth groups lie on the red, low-star-forming sequence and correspond to environmentally quenched and mass-quenched systems, respectively, while the sixth group traces the massive end of the star-forming sequence, and the seventh group appears to represent a more heterogeneous population that may include transition objects. The remaining groups populate the low- to intermediate-mass blue sequence, including both compact and more extended star-forming galaxies. The second MOBSynC stage merges the simple clusters into two compound groups: a red sequence formed by the third and the fourth groups, and the rest merging to form a broad blue sequence. Our results show that the familiar red-blue bimodality of local galaxies contains additional physically meaningful substructure linked to quenching pathway, morphology, and environment.

AI.tldr: The paper uses a t-mixture of factor analysers (MtFAD) with syncytial clustering (MOBSynC) to classify 5,306 GAMA galaxies, revealing that the classic red-blue bimodality contains physically meaningful substructure related to quenching, morphology, and environment.
AI.motivation: Galaxy classification needs to jointly account for internal properties and environment, but traditional distance-based unsupervised clustering fails to handle heavy-tailed distributions, feature dependencies, and probabilistic characterization.
AI.method: Apply t-mixture of factor analysers with group-specific latent structures (MtFAD) for probabilistic modeling, followed by model-estimated overlap-based syncytial clustering (MOBSynC) to merge weakly separated groups into higher-level structures.
AI.result: Eight simple clusters identified: groups 3-4 = red, low-star-forming (environmentally vs. mass-quenched); group 6 = massive star-forming; group 7 = heterogeneous/transition; remainder = low-to-intermediate mass blue sequence. MOBSynC merges into red sequence (groups 3+4) and broad blue sequence (others).
AI.conclusion: The familiar red-blue bimodality contains additional physically meaningful substructure linked to quenching pathway, morphology, and environment, demonstrating that probabilistic factor-analyzer mixture models with syncytial merging outperform traditional clustering for galaxy population studies.

title: The FAST Hundred-Deg$^2$ HI Deep (HD$^2$) Survey: Early Results from the Pilot Survey
comment: 26 pages, 14 figures, accepted by ApJS. Table 5 can be downloaded from the survey website at https://ccg-fast.github.io/
summary: The Hundred-deg$^2$ HI Deep (HD$^2$) survey carried out with the Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical Telescope (FAST) is planned to map a contiguous region within the DESI DR1 footprint, achieving an effective integration time of 20 minutes for each pointing and a uniform detection sensitivity of 0.28 mJy beam$^{-1}$ at 4.8 km s$^{-1}$ resolution. We present early results from the pilot HD$^2$ survey: a 10 deg$^2$ field overlapping with HSC-SSP and the DESI EDR SV3, observed with an integration time of 7.3 minutes per beam and the rms of 0.45 mJy beam$^{-1}$ at 4.8 km s$^{-1}$ resolution. We identify 339 HI sources at $z<0.09$, corresponding to $\sim$34 detections per deg$^2$, nearly six times higher than the detection rate of the wide-field surveys. Optical counterparts are primarily identified using DESI redshifts, yielding a matching rate and correctness exceeding 90% for galaxies with $r<19.5$ mag, a substantial improvement over SDSS. Under the constraint of $r < 17.8$ mag and $0.01 < z < 0.05$, nearly 50% of galaxies in the DESI BGS samples have HI detections in this pilot survey. The optical properties of these HI-detected galaxies span nearly the entire parameter range of the DESI sample. The gas fraction scaling relations versus stellar mass, stellar mass surface density, NUV-r, and specific star formation rate are consistent with previous surveys, e.g., ALFALFA, DINGO, and xGASS. These results justify the feasibility of the full HD$^2$ survey, which will build a high-completeness HI census over a contiguous area to probe the cold gas scaling relations of galaxies over different scales.

AI.tldr: The HD² survey uses FAST to map neutral hydrogen (HI) in a large sky region. A pilot 10 deg² field detected 339 HI sources at z<0.09 (~34 detections/deg², 6× higher than wide surveys), with >90% optical matching rate for r<19.5 mag galaxies using DESI redshifts. Gas fraction scaling relations are consistent with ALFALFA, DINGO, and xGASS, validating the feasibility of the full survey.
AI.motivation: To map a contiguous, high-sensitivity HI survey using FAST, achieving higher detection rates and completeness than previous wide-field surveys, and to build a high-completeness HI census for studying cold gas scaling relations across different galaxy scales.
AI.method: Pilot HD² survey of a 10 deg² field with FAST (7.3 min/beam integration, 0.45 mJy/beam rms at 4.8 km/s resolution); optical counterparts identified primarily via DESI redshifts.
AI.result: 339 HI sources detected at z<0.09 (~34 detections/deg²); >90% matching rate and correctness for r<19.5 mag galaxies; ~50% of DESI BGS galaxies with r<17.8 mag and 0.01<z<0.05 have HI detections; gas fraction scaling relations consistent with ALFALFA, DINGO, xGASS.
AI.conclusion: The pilot survey demonstrates feasibility of the full HD² survey, which will provide a high-completeness HI census over a contiguous area to probe cold gas scaling relations of galaxies.

title: Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus: Lithium evolution from early red-giant-branch and main-sequence stars
comment: 7 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: The combination of data from the Gaia satellite and large ground-based spectroscopic surveys recently lead to a milestone understanding of our Galaxy's formation history, marked by the identification of stellar remnants of the accreted Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) dwarf galaxy. Lithium (Li) remains one of the most difficult elements to explain because of its complex behaviour over evolutionary timescales: both the Spite plateau observed in metal-poor main-sequence (MS) stars and the recently discovered Li plateau of early red-giant-branch (eRGB) stars in the Milky Way challenge current galactic chemical evolution models. In this article, we investigate the viability of these Li-plateau features in the GSE galaxy, using public data from current big surveys: GALAH, Gaia-ESO, and the collective SAGA database. We present a chemical evolution model of Li for GSE and find agreement with the observed data. We find the signature of Li plateau at low metallicities in both eRGB and MS stars. At higher metallicities, we see candidates of the Li-enriched stars that have their main contribution from nova explosions. These results reinforce the universality of the Spite plateau, and indicate that the eRGB Li plateau might also be a universal feature across different galactic systems. A hint of low nova Li yield in GSE is suggested by our eRGB sample from GALAH. However, the lack of stars at high metallicities, possibly caused by the merger event, prevents a precise study of nova contributions, and we expect that upcoming data will enable a more comprehensive analysis.

AI.tldr: This paper investigates lithium plateaus (Spite plateau in main-sequence stars and the recently discovered eRGB plateau) in the Gaia-Sausage-Enceladus (GSE) dwarf galaxy using data from GALAH, Gaia-ESO, and SAGA. A chemical evolution model for Li in GSE is developed, showing agreement with observed data. The results support universality of both Li plateaus across galactic systems and suggest low nova Li yield in GSE.
AI.motivation: To investigate whether the Spite plateau and the newly discovered eRGB Li plateau observed in the Milky Way are universal features present also in the accreted GSE dwarf galaxy, and to constrain lithium chemical evolution models across galactic systems.
AI.method: Used public spectroscopic data from GALAH, Gaia-ESO, and SAGA databases to analyze Li abundances in GSE stars. Developed a chemical evolution model for lithium tailored to the GSE system and compared model predictions with observed Li plateaus in both main-sequence and early red-giant-branch stars across metallicity ranges.
AI.result: Found signature of the Li plateau at low metallicities in both eRGB and MS stars. At higher metallicities, identified candidates of Li-enriched stars likely contributed by nova explosions. The eRGB sample from GALAH suggests a hint of low nova Li yield in GSE. The lack of high-metallicity stars (likely due to the merger event) limits precise study of nova contributions.
AI.conclusion: Reinforces the universality of the Spite plateau and suggests the eRGB Li plateau may also be a universal feature across different galactic systems. Highlights the need for future data to enable more comprehensive analysis of nova contributions at high metallicities.
